title: SLA Charter & Elasticity Intent — Guided Intake Template for Dedicated Reservations
creator: Maya Green
description:
Background:
Customers requesting Dedicated (reserved GPU) capacity frequently arrive with partial or inconsistent information about their required SLA targets, expected traffic patterns, and scaling tolerance. This causes long back-and-forth during onboarding and incorrect pool sizing that either wastes capacity or causes missed SLOs.

Goal:
Create a guided intake template and accompanying negotiation script that enables Solutions Engineering and Sales to capture a consistent 'SLA charter' and 'elasticity intent' from customers during the initial qualifying conversation. The output will feed the capacity recommender and the Dedicated onboarding workflow.

Scope:
- A single-page intake form (spreadsheet + structured fields) for frontline teams.
- A short decision rubric that maps customer statements to 'reserved throughput' buckets, GPU family recommendations (perf vs cost), and fallback/autoscale policies.
- Templates for sales/solutions to confirm contractual SLA language (latency P95/P99, availability, throttling behavior) and operational runbooks.
- Integration points: onboarding tracker (Sheet/Notion), capacity recommender API (PM-1002345), and Console rollout policies.

Non-Goals:
- Implementing autoscale engine changes (out of scope; handled by ENG roadmap).
- Final legal contract text (we'll provide standard clauses for review).

Proposed Intake Fields (minimal set):
1) Business context (use case, regulatory constraints)
2) Peak QPS and 95th/99th token latency targets
3) Average sequence length and distribution (p90/p99 tokens)
4) Expected concurrency and burst patterns (sustained vs spiky)
5) Model family / open model compatibility and required quantization level
6) Acceptable fallback model classes and graceful degradation behavior
7) Data residency & encryption requirements
8) Billing model preference (committed monthly, committed annual, burst credits)
9) Operational contact and escalation cadence

Decision Rubric (high level):
- If latency target <= 200ms P95 for gen workloads and bursty traffic -> recommend GPU family X (high-perf) + reserved throughput band A.
- If customer allows relaxed latency (>= 500ms P95) or batched workloads -> recommend cost-optimized GPU family Y + band C with larger batching.
- If regulatory constraint: private deployment/VPC required -> route to Private onboarding with dedicated SLA ladder and security checklist.
- If traffic shows predictable diurnal pattern -> use preferred autoscale windows and smaller reserved baseline.

Deliverables:
- One-pager intake template (CSV/Notion template)
- Negotiation script with example phrasings for common push/pull decisions
- Mapping table that outputs: recommended reserved throughput, GPU family, default autoscale policy, and suggested contractual SLA banding
- Quick training deck for Solutions/AE teams (20min)

Acceptance criteria:
- Frontline teams can fill the intake form end-to-end in a 15-minute customer call and get a deterministic recommendation from the mapping table.
- The mapping table aligns with capacity recommender API inputs (PM-1002345) and reduces follow-ups by >=50% in pilot.
- Pilot with 3 enterprise customers scheduled and signed off by Solutions Eng.

Metrics to measure success:
- Reduction in average onboarding loop time (days)
- % of intake forms with complete fields after first call
- Change in accuracy of initial pool sizing (measured vs actual first-2-weeks utilization)

Notes on trade-offs and decisions:
- Conservative sizing reduces immediate outages but increases committed cost for customers; include explicit 'cost-vs-availability' checkbox in intake.
- Defaulting to higher perf GPUs for hard latency SLAs simplifies guarantees but may be overkill for some RLHF workflows; require model fingerprinting questions.
- For early pilots we'll err on the side of availability for customers with high reputational risk.

Artifacts and links:
- Intake draft (Notion): https://confluence.redwood.company/dedicated-intake/one-pager
- Capacity recommender API spec: https://docs.redwood.company/capacity-recommender/spec
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake template available in Notion + CSV export; 2) Mapping table produces clear recommendation for reserved throughput and GPU family without manual tweaks; 3) Pilot scheduled with 3 customers and pilot retrospective notes captured; 4) Solutions Eng reports >50% fewer follow-ups for sizing questions.
